text:
I cannot remember

why I chose that kingdom of brick.

Why the corner so damp, the green

corner of the corridor?

Only terror passed by, sometimes

the insolent figure devoured

almost at once by the light.

I was always alone, at least

as far as I remember. When she came in

she seemed barefoot to me,

her bare skin tall in the shaken half-light.


The airs up to the ceiling

were dyed with her, and everything smelled

of nocturnal animal;

I myself was her smell, I myself

almost like her foam.


She did not pass by again.

Her body remained in me, the certainty

beneath all clothing.


She broke the hours of doing nothing,

sowed the instrumental and white world

with fear, among fears.

translation.title: I Cannot Remember...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Barral's memory of a single apparition altering a sterile, fearful interior.
